title: se-implementation-scratchpad-amberwood-financial
content:
Goal: get Amberwood Financial on Redwood Private (VPC) POC. Notes + action items from customer call and initial infra run.

High-level customer asks / constraints:
- Regulated banking: data cannot leave their VPC.
- Prefer on-prem managed gateway for HSM / KMS integration (AWS account 734210998712).
- Target latency: 95p < 120ms for chat use-case (avg request size ~120 tokens).
- Throughput: 50 concurrent chats, burst to 120.
- Models: want to serve redwood/llm-small quantized (4-bit) for now; may add llama2-70b later on Dedicated.

Quick infra notes / values collected:
- VPC CIDR: 10.10.0.0/16 (customer provided)
- Subnets: public: 10.10.0.0/24, private-1: 10.10.1.0/24, private-2: 10.10.2.0/24
- AWS account: 734210998712 (IAM contact: @maria-fernandez (Amberwood))
- KMS key alias: alias/amberwood-redwood (customer will create HSM-backed key)
- Allowed egress: outbound to Redwood control-plane only on TLS 443 -> redwood-control.redwood.ai (will confirm exact IPs)
- VPN: IPSec candidate; open question re: port 500/4500 policies through their edge firewall

Initial POC machine sizing (suggested):
- 2x g5.12xlarge equiv (NVIDIA H100) for model serving (replicas=2) with 64GB KV cache per node
- Min replicas: 1, Max: 4 (autoscale based on concurrency & CPU/GPU util)
- Batch window: 20ms for chat (experiment with 10/30ms)
- Suggested quantization: nf4_4bit (we tested earlier with similar workload)

Local quick tests (on staging infra) - 2026-02-12:
- Model: redwood/llm-small-quant4 (approx 4-bit)
- Sequence: prompt ~120 tokens, generate 80 tokens
- Measured p50: 48ms; p95: 128ms (single node, batch size=1) -> need to improve p95 to hit 120ms SLO
- With batching (batch size=4) p50: 52ms, p95: 96ms (but tail depends on queueing)
- KV cache hit for prefix-heavy traffic cuts cost ~30% (enable prefix caching at route level)

Risks / open questions (to resolve with Amberwood):
- Firewall: do they allow persistent TLS connections to Redwood control plane? If not, need alternate connector (outbound-only tunnel)
- KMS/HSM: customer wants HSM; confirm algorithm support and latency for signing keys -> might affect startup times for containers
- Model pinning & updates: who signs off on model/quantization changes in prod? Needs governance flow (CS + legal + Amberwood ops)
- SLA requirements: they asked for 99.95% uptime during business hours; need to map to Dedicated + multi-az setup or private HA recommendation

Immediate action items (owner - due):
- A1: Send network checklist to Amberwood (include required egress IPs/ports + VPN options) - owner: Noah Patel - due: 2026-03-03
- A2: Confirm KMS/HSM compatibility matrix and required latency impacts - owner: Ava Martinez - due: 2026-03-06
- A3: Run 3-node perf test (g5x3) with quant4 and increased concurrency to reproduce p95 tail - owner: Maya Singh - due: 2026-03-05
- A4: Draft preliminary rollback plan and canary config for model updates (A/B traffic split + automatic fallback to smaller model) - owner: Rachel Kim - due: 2026-03-08
- A5: Add Amberwood to internal SOC review queue and attach compliance checklist - owner: Solutions Eng ops - due: 2026-03-10

Notes for onboarding runbook (to be formalized into Confluence):
- Step 0: Exchange AWS cross-account role ARN and create limited-role for Redwood control plane ops
- Step 1: Validate network egress and route tables (test tunnel if VPN chosen)
- Step 2: Provision KMS alias and provide key ARN to Redwood (attach appropriate grants)
- Step 3: Deploy control-plane connector inside Amberwood VPC (helm chart: redwood-connector v1.4.2)
- Step 4: Push initial model bundle (redwood/llm-small-quant4) and start canary (5% traffic) for 24h
- Step 5: Run evals against customer's prompt set (we have 50 golden prompts) and compare embedding similarity + hallucination rates

Slack threads / refs:
- slack: #se-amberwood-onboarding (pinned: checklist, infra diagram)
- convo: https://redwood.slack.com/archives/SES12345 (internal thread)

Short-term reminders (personal):
- 1) Bring up perf infra by 2026-03-03 (need docker images from release-engineering - PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/release-engineering/pull/412)
- 2) Prep short demo (5-7 min) showing failover from private -> hosted fallback (for exec call 2026-03-09)
- 3) Check with legal on data residency clause before enabling persistent logs (I/O to S3)

Conversation snippets / quick thoughts (raw):
- "They want everything in-VPC but also want us to manage updates. Tradeoff: more operational overhead for us or provide a control plane agent that they fully own."
- "If firewall blocks outbound, consider using an outbound-only connector deployed into their DMZ that polls for control commands. Avoid inbound ports."

End of scratchpad. Will copy critical items into Confluence page once A1/A2 done and we have network answers.
